finding.claim: The /settings/email state-changing endpoint uses @login_optional instead of @login_required. Unauthenticated requests reach set_email with g.uid = None. This is a missing authentication check on an account-modifying operation. The sibling /settings/password route correctly uses @login_required, which suggests the wrong decorator was applied here.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to /settings/email with no session cookie
finding.sink: set_email(g.uid, ...) at routes.py:37, which changes an account email

trace.note: login_optional sets g.uid = session.get('uid') (None if anonymous) and never aborts

set_email(g.uid, ...) runs for anonymous callers. If set_email treats a None uid as a no-op, the call does nothing. If it treats None as a wildcard or an unscoped query, it could update the wrong or all accounts. Its body is a stub, so this can't be confirmed from this file.

finding.guards_checked: login_required is not applied to this route. There is no inline session check in change_email. There is no CSRF protection anywhere in the app. before_request hooks: none. Other files: none exist in the directory. The set_email stub has no uid validation. Impact depends on the real set_email implementation. The missing authentication check is certain, but the exploitable effect cannot be confirmed from this file.
